title: Asking about a contrast the text states
statement: How can an open question ask about a contrast the text states outright without giving the answer away, when naming both sides nearly states it?
example: All three judged drafts of one such question named both sides of the contrast and were judged give-aways, at 0.69, 0.71 and 0.65.
detail: In the 12 October run the open check on a speech built around a contrast it states outright was drafted three times. Every draft named both sides of the contrast and a word for lasting, endurance or durability, and the give-away check said yes each time (0.69, 0.71, 0.65), so the block failed and no wording that passes was produced.
against: The give-away check has no person-labelled cases, so it is not settled that these questions do give the answer away.

evidence.quote: "q": "What difference does the speaker draw between the endurance of the ceremony and the impact of the fighting?",
"q": "How does the speaker contrast the durability of what the soldiers did with the durability of the speech?",
"q": "What difference does the speaker draw between the endurance of spoken words and the actions of the soldiers?",
"The question does not give its answer away: the judge found this does not hold"
